Gauge repeatability and reproducibility of an LLM pipeline

Source: R/grr.R
msa_grr.Rd

Turns the variance components of an msa_fit() into the statistics that a measurement-system analysis reports. The vocabulary follows the AIAG Measurement Systems Analysis manual:

Usage

msa_grr(fit, threshold = NULL, basis = c("study_var", "contribution"))

Arguments

fit

An msa_fit.

threshold

Length-two vector of thresholds (acceptable / marginal) on the chosen basis, in percent.

basis

"study_var" classifies by percent study variation (default, thresholds 10 and 30), "contribution" by percent contribution (typical thresholds 1 and 9).

Value

An object of class msa_grr with elements table (one row per source), summary (named vector: grr_pct_study_var, grr_pct_contribution, repeatability_pct_study_var, reproducibility_pct_study_var, ndc, icc_items), verdict, the thresholds and the outcome type.

Details

  • Repeatability: the residual variance, i.e. variation between replicate calls under identical conditions (same item, prompt, model).

  • Reproducibility: variation attributable to the measurement conditions, here prompt variant, model, block (time) and their interactions with each other and with the items.

  • Total gauge R&R: repeatability + reproducibility, the variance the pipeline adds to a result.

  • Part-to-part: the variance between items, the signal the pipeline is meant to resolve.

Two ratios are reported for every source: the percent contribution (variance / total variance) and the percent study variation (standard deviation / total standard deviation). The AIAG rule of thumb classifies a system by the percent study variation of total gauge R&R: below 10 % acceptable, 10-30 % marginal (may be acceptable depending on the application, cost and risk), above 30 % unacceptable. The number of distinct categories (ndc) is floor(1.41 * sd_items / sd_grr); a system should resolve at least 5. Thresholds should be set from the model risk of the context of use, not taken as universal constants.

Examples

g <- msa_grr(msa_fit(ic50_demo, type = "numeric"))
g
#> Gauge R&R of an LLM measurement system
#>   outcome: numeric; 40 items x 3 prompts x 3 models x 2 block(s), 2152 observations
#>  Source               Variance SD     % Contribution % Study Var
#>  Total gauge R&R      0.0425   0.2061 4.2 %          20.5 %     
#>    Repeatability      0.0140   0.1184 1.4 %          11.8 %     
#>    Reproducibility    0.0285   0.1687 2.8 %          16.8 %     
#>      prompt           0.0049   0.0697 0.5 %          6.9 %      
#>      model            0.0171   0.1309 1.7 %          13.0 %     
#>      block (time)     0.0010   0.0319 0.1 %          3.2 %      
#>      prompt:model     0.0000   0.0046 0.0 %          0.5 %      
#>      item:prompt      0.0001   0.0092 0.0 %          0.9 %      
#>      item:model       0.0054   0.0731 0.5 %          7.3 %      
#>  Part-to-part (items) 0.9672   0.9834 95.8 %         97.9 %     
#>  Total variation      1.0096   1.0048 100.0 %        100.0 %    
#> 
#>   total gauge R&R: 20.5 % of study variation (4.2 % contribution)
#>   number of distinct categories (ndc): 6
#>   ICC (items): 0.958
#>   verdict: MARGINAL  [basis: % study variation, thresholds 10 / 30]
g$summary
